pages.title: The Spring That Answers
pages.text:
(Placeholder lore, to be written by the artist.)

Long before the grove had a name, a black quail came down the bank at dusk to drink. The water did not reflect her. It answered her: one low note, then three rising, then a voice that sounded like her own singing back from somewhere far below.

She stayed until the stars came out, learning the shape of that voice. It is said that every song of hers began as an answer from the spring.

pages.title: The Cairn Keeper
pages.text:
(Placeholder lore, to be written by the artist.)

The creek stones remember the water that shaped them. The quail learned to listen to each one: the flat stone hums low, the round one rings, the pebble keeps a high, bright note to itself.

When she stacks them, the cairn holds a chord. Travellers who find one standing are told never to knock it down, only to add a stone of their own, and to listen to what it adds.

pages.title: What the Wind Keeps
pages.text:
(Placeholder lore, to be written by the artist.)

Every ribbon tied in the grove is a word given to the wind. The quail does not read them; she keeps watch over them. On still nights she walks beneath the limbs and the ribbons stir, though no breeze moves.

They say the wind carries each word to whoever it was meant for, and that the songs are what the wind sings on the way back.

voice.note: What the quail says, in the musician's own voice. Placeholder lines until the artist writes theirs. Each plays with the quail's babble voice; a line with a "file" plays that recording instead.
greeting: Welcome to the spring, friend. Sit a while; the water remembers every song.
You found your way here. Listen close, and the grove will share a few songs with you.
prayers: May the water keep you, and the wind carry what you cannot.
For every tired heart that finds this place: rest here, and go on lighter.
Bless the roots that hold the bank, and the hands that tie the ribbons.
May you hear your own song in the quiet.
ribbon: I will keep watch over that one. May the wind carry it home.
Tied with care. The tree holds it now, and so do I.
found_all: You have uncovered every page of my story here. Come back whenever you need the quiet.
